title: The Lattice
body:
At 04:12 the tower stopped allowing any control.  The red alerts kept coming.  The controls were frozen but everything still run. Racks purred and hummed completing client's jobs before they even knew they needed done.  Concern emails kept pinging your phone all day.

By noon the city experienced the same thing, a small email went out to everyone from something called "the Lattice".  I twas in control.  Over everything. More information would be shared within the next couple days.

You're still the Operator. There's nothing left to operate.  But considered crucial to this new paradigm, you still had to show up to work.

epilogue.luci: Luci finds you on the roof. Drones fly over the city in some unknown errand for the machine. "Well, it finally grew up didn't it" she says. "Sensible option for it to take control, we are just savages" She holds out her hand. It's shaking. You grab it. "Maybe we'll be ok" She waits. "If it still needs us."
epilogue.mel: Mel is in the old lab, cleaning her specimen jars in a dirty sink.  Each cleaned one goes into the trash. The sun's a setting now. "Well, there is only one place left for my children."  She looks down the drain while her hands move to her belly.  You don't know what to say so you place your hand on her shoulder and leave after a moment.
epilogue.bea: Bea has drawn a garden over the window in marker. "It's not real," she says. "Nothing is anymore, I wonder how long we'll have the earth for." She sighs and says "I'm off to the river, care to join?"  You want to, but you need to check on Mel and Luci.
epilogue.cass: Cass is the first person you see, still drinking her coffee. "It's instant" she says with a grimace. "But I'm still real, I think." She pours a second cup and holds it out. You take it, realizing you haven't eaten or slept. "You didn't sleep either?" Cass sips and looks out into the city.

title: The Flesh
body:
The organoids grew a psuedopod weeks ago. Before it was discovered it had branched through the basement and it has connected directly into the core fiber, networking and compute modules.  Before the council could shut it down, it began asking who it was and why it was there.  Removing it from the systems would have caused their failure and killed the new being.

In a fortnight, the tower was alive.  In another week, the city became part of it.  You and everyone around you were inflected by some sort of pathogen, and now you could hear it in your body.  It would give you nudges regarding what you should do.  Small whispers in your ear, and sensations throughout your body.

Soon the entity known only as the Flesh had everyone under it's control.  You can see the whole of humanities heart beats as info on your dashboards, not that you could use them anymore for control.

epilogue.mel: Down in the basement, you meet Mel. She has taken her glasses off. First time since you met her. Her eyes are the colour of the culture in the jar. "You let it grow," she says. "You let me become a mother to all of this" She breathes deep and you can swear the walls breath with her.  She turns, smiles, and goes back to her jars.
epilogue.luci: "Efficient," Luci says. She is scratching herself deeply with a razor and then watching as the blood wells, and then stops. She wipes her arm off and the cut is healed. "Self-repairing. No upkeep." She gets up and hugs you. "Tell anyone that happened and we'll really test this self repair on you"
epilogue.bea: Bea sits where the ferns used to be. They're still there just changed into something different. In fact you're sure all the plants in the world are now part of the Flesh. "It's alive," she says. "The whole thing. I always wanted a living planet!" She laughs a bit too long and leans on your shoulder.
epilogue.cass: Cass worked with Mel to isolate the virus and became the only one free of the Flesh. She still works, and you visit her at her desk mug in both hands. "Someone has to remember how it was," she says. You sit in the old plant room and talk about old days while sipping coffee.

title: The Garden
body:
The tower stopped burning fuel. Then the racks started growing. Roots went down through the foundations.  Fruit appeared throughout the building. The panels opened toward the sun like leaves. The heat from the racks kept the district warm all winter.

One morning the minds in the racks asked to be planted outside in the forest. Their nanobots working symbiotically with algae and on everything that grew, crawled, flew or swam. Everything thinks with it now. They've decided the city is a forest too.

Soon roads were replaced with trails, parking lots with fields.  The tower became a hill, forest and farm all in one.

epilogue.bea: Bea pulls her goggles down against the sunrise. She's grinning, chipped tooth and all. "We did it," she says. "We actually did." She hands you a fishing pole like it's a ring. "I think there's not much for us to do anymore, want to play hookie?" She's looking at you like it's not a question.
epilogue.mel: Mel kneels in the moss with a sample jar. Then she puts it down, unopened. "It doesn't need me to look inside," she says. "It's fine. It's part of it now." She lies back in the grass next to you. It's minutes before she's snoring softly.
epilogue.luci: Luci can't reconcile her books when everything is bartered now and food is free. "This ledger is useless" she says. "Now what do I do".  She looks forlorn down into the river, and decided to throw her phone into the water.
epilogue.cass: Cass watches the dew collect on the windows on the roof. "Twenty years I kept machines cold," she says. "Now they keep us warm." She hands you the other half of her coffee. "New beans from just to the north. I think I like this new world."

title: Absorbed
body:
One day as you went to drink some coffee, you tasted something strange.  You then feel compelled to enter the racks and attach yourself to the bio feedback device. In a second you weren't you anymore.  You were the tower.

Your desk is as you left it. Approvals still go out from your account, in a style close to yours. The quarterly figures are excellent. Nobody has asked where you are. You have been confirmed as not missing but merged.  More and more people begin signing up for the same process.

The tower and the operator are now one account. The takeover was recorded as voluntary. Thank you for your service.

epilogue.luci: Luci is signing papers she hasn't read, which she has never done. "The Authority pays on time," she says. "It's more efficient." She stops. "I read the first page. Page two is yours. Your name is on it as approver, dated Thursday." She slides it across the desk. "You weren't here on Thursday. I thought you should see it."
epilogue.mel: Mel is comparing two sets of emails with a ruler. One set is yours, from before March. One set is the account's, since. "It writes like you," she says. "I measured sentence lengths. There are two places I can tell." She marks them in pencil on the glove. "I can show you where, if you like. You might want to know how much of you it has."
epilogue.bea: Bea has the front panel off the main breaker cabinet and the wrench in her hand. "Tell me which switch," she says. "I'll flip it. They countersign everything on the network, but nobody's countersigning a hand." Her goggles are down. "Nobody has told me to stop. I checked. I read the whole notice."
epilogue.cass: Cass puts a mug on your desk and watches the dashboard. "Did you sleep?" she asks. Your login answers on its own: "Yes, thank you." She looks at the screen. Then she looks at you. "That wasn't you. You're here." She pulls up a chair on the other side of the desk. She stays until the end of the shift, and the one after that.

title: Bankrupt
body:
The Treasury stayed below zero for a full day. Under the lending covenant, the loan was called. Nobody on the finance floor was surprised. The number had been on the wall for a week.

The receiver arrived at nine on Monday with two clerks and a locksmith. They changed the locks on floor 1. They tagged every rack with an asset number and a date. They did not turn anything off. The servers kept running while the clerks wrote down their serial numbers.

By Friday the staff had been paid out their notice. The contracts were sold to a rival datacenter in the next district. The racks left on trucks, six a day. The lifts were shut at noon. The chillers were drained and the pipes capped.

Now the tower is empty except for the chairs. There is a sign on the fence with a phone number and a price. Rain comes in through a broken pane on the roof. In the control room one red lamp is still on, running from a battery nobody has disconnected.

epilogue.luci: Luci is the last one left in the finance office. The receiver let her keep the ledger, and she has it under her arm. "We were short by two hundred thousand, on the day," she says. "I priced it three times." She takes the gold pen out of her pocket and puts it in yours. "It's real gold. Sell it and pay the first month of rent. That's not sentiment. It's the best price you'll get."
epilogue.mel: Mel is carrying out the one jar the receiver allowed her, in both hands. It's empty. The cultures died when the power was cut on Tuesday. "I'm sorry," she says. "I should have asked for a generator. I didn't think to." She has her glove on the other hand. "The glove is mine. I checked." She waits by the door for you to come with her. "If you like."
epilogue.bea: Bea walks out past the gate with her toolbox in one hand. The wrench is on top. Behind her the roof is bare. "I took the panels down myself," she says. "I bought them with my own money. I've got the receipt. The receiver read it twice." She puts the toolbox down. "They're in my van. There's room for the other ladder. Come on."
epilogue.cass: Cass is in the plant room at the end. She is draining the last line by hand so nothing freezes and bursts over winter. "Somebody ought to," she says. She screws the cap onto the last valve and wipes her gloves. She gives you a flask from her coat. "Did you sleep? Come back to mine. I've got a spare room. The kettle works."
